samples.summary: Slides mobile toolbar's duplicated B/I/U toggle logic changed with no test
samples.evidence: `TextEditMobileBar` carries its own copy of the bold/italic/underline toggle + pressed-state logic (now reading `getRangeStyleSummary()` via `isStyleOn`). The diff adds dedicated regression tests for the other two copies of this logic (`tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` for the shared `TextFormatGroup`, `tests/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx` for the docs slim toolbar) but none for this one. Grepping packages/frontend/tests for `mobile-toolbar`/`TextEditMobileBar` returns no files, so nothing pins that this third copy inverts the range value rather than the caret value — it can silently regress to the caret-based bug.
searchedFor: Grep 'isStyleOn' across packages/frontend (only src files, no tests)

samples.summary: ~100 lines of new range-walk branches in isStyleOnInSelection (table cell range, cross-block, cross-block-inside-cell) are untested
samples.evidence: The new `isStyleOnInSelection` has four distinct traversal branches: `range.tableCellRange` rectangle, same-block, cross-block-within-one-cell, and top-level cross-block (with cell-endpoint normalization, colSpan===0 skipping, `visitTable`). The only new engine test (packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts) uses a single paragraph with two inline runs and one block id, exercising *only* the same-block branch. Grepping packages/docs/test for `tableCellRange` shows existing usages in unrelated tests (table-merge-context, cell-range-expand, editor-step-selection-font-size) — none dispatch a Cmd+B / toggleStyle over a cell range or a multi-block range, so a wrong index/offset in those branches would ship green.

samples.summary: Documented mixed-range and no-text-run fallback semantics of the new engine helper are only covered by frontend mocks, not by the real editor
samples.evidence: The doc comment on `isStyleOnInSelection` states two behaviours: a mixed range (some runs on, some off) counts as not applied so the next press styles the whole range, and `undefined` is returned when the range holds no text runs so the caller falls back to the caret style. The new engine test only covers uniformly-unstyled and uniformly-styled ranges (setupEditor(true,false) / (false,true) / (true,true)); no test selects a range spanning one bold and one non-bold run, nor an empty/zero-width-run range. The 'mixed' assertions in the frontend tests feed a hard-coded `{key: 'mixed'}` stub summary, so they cannot detect the engine computing the wrong value.
searchedFor: Grep 'mixed' in packages/docs/test (11 files; none is the new toggle test)
Read of the new backward-selection-toggle test
Read of the frontend text-format-toggles and header/footer tests (mocked summaries)

samples.summary: Only Cmd+B is exercised at the engine level; the italic/underline/strikethrough keyboard shortcuts named in the fix are not
samples.evidence: `isStyleOnInSelection`'s doc comment explicitly covers Cmd/Ctrl+B, I, U and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+X (strikethrough). `dispatchKey` is only ever called with 'b'; no test dispatches 'i', 'u' or shift+'x'. If any of those shortcut handlers still routes through the caret style instead of `toggleStyle`/the new range read, the suite stays green. (Lower severity because the shared code path is covered via bold.)
searchedFor: Read of the new test file (only dispatchKey(container,'b'))

finding.evidence: `TextEditMobileBar` carries its own copy of the bold/italic/underline toggle + pressed-state logic (now reading `getRangeStyleSummary()` via `isStyleOn`). The diff adds dedicated regression tests for the other two copies of this logic (`tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` for the shared `TextFormatGroup`, `tests/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx` for the docs slim toolbar) but none for this one. searchedFor: Grep 'isStyleOn' across packages/frontend (only src files, no tests)

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `TextEditMobileBar` holds its own inline B/I/U toggle logic reading `getRangeStyleSummary()` via `isStyleOn` (mobile-toolbar.tsx:229-244 for the actions, :252/:260/:268 for pressed state), not delegated to the shared `TextFormatGroup`. Repo-wide greps for `mobile-toolbar` / `TextEditMobileBar` (hidden dirs included, as .agent-review hits show) return only the source file, toolbar/index.tsx, and docs — no test file and no test that imports `@/app/slides/toolbar` (only shared-document.tsx and the visual harness). I searched BOTH test trees, since this package colocates tests in src/ (src/app/slides/toolbar/arrange-menu.test.tsx exists) as well as packages/frontend/tests; neither has a mobile-toolbar test. tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts only mounts `TextFormatGroup`, and the docs header/footer test only covers the docs slim toolbar, so neither can fail if the mobile copy regresses to caret-based toggling. The only mobile artifacts are pixel baselines under tests/visual/baselines, which cannot distinguish caret-vs-range semantics, and the harness `slides-toolbar-text-editing` scenario is a desktop screenshot stub. The task doc itself marks the mobile swap as part of this change (line 55-57) while listing regression tests only for the other two copies. A changed behavior with no meaningful test is major under the test-adequacy rubric; found no counterexample.

finding.summary: The header/footer slim toolbar's B/I/U toggles were changed the same way but have no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff duplicates the fix (not reusing TextFormatGroup) in the `isHeaderFooter` branch of docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx (lines 391–406). The new test file only mounts `TextFormatGroup` (packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts:99), and grepping the frontend test tree for `DocsFormattingToolbar` / `isHeaderFooter` returns zero test files (only src files: shared-document.tsx, harness/hunt/page.tsx, docs-detail.tsx, App.tsx, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx). So this second, hand-copied copy of the toggle logic could regress (e.g. reverting to `getSelectionStyle()`, or dropping `isStyleOn` so `'mixed'` becomes truthy) with the suite still green. Note also that these slim toggles pass no `pressed` prop, so no test could even observe their state.

verdict.reason: A dedicated test file for the header/footer slim toolbar B/I/U toggles exists and actually runs, so the "no test at all" claim is false. packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx imports DocsFormattingToolbar (line 15), mounts it with editContext 'header'/'footer' (lines 55-61) against a stubbed EditorAPI whose getSelectionStyle() and getRangeStyleSummary() deliberately disagree (lines 35-53), clicks the slim toggles by aria-label "Bold"/"Italic"/"Underline" — the exact labels on the isHeaderFooter branch buttons (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:449, 458, 467) — and asserts the resulting applyStyle payload. The assertions are non-vacuous and catch both regressions the reviewer feared: the "range unstyled but caret styled" and "range uniformly styled" cases (test lines 71-87) fail if the code reverted to getSelectionStyle(), and the 'mixed' case (lines 89-96, expects {key: true} when the summary is 'mixed') fails if isStyleOn were dropped, since !'mixed' is false. The file matches the vitest include globs tests/**/*.test.tsx (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:268), so it is part of the suite. The reviewer's grep evidence is inaccurate — this file does contain DocsFormattingToolbar. The secondary note about the slim toggles passing no pressed prop concerns rendering/design of non-test code, outside this lens and not a coverage gap in the toggle logic itself.

searchedFor: Grep backward|reverse|anchor in that test file
finding.summary: The bug being fixed (backward selection) is only ever asserted by a mock that hardcodes the desired answer; nothing tests that getRangeStyleSummary is actually correct for a backward selection
finding.evidence: `makeEditor` stubs `getRangeStyleSummary: vi.fn(() => summary)` with the value the test wants (line 41), so the tests prove only "the component reads the summary and applies !isStyleOn" — the entire premise of the fix (that a backward/right-to-left selection makes `getSelectionStyle()` report the preceding run while `getRangeStyleSummary()` reports the range correctly) is asserted nowhere. In packages/docs/test/view/editor-range-style-summary.test.ts every `_setSelectionForTest` call uses a forward range (anchor offset <= focus offset: lines 101-104, 124-127, 144-147, 167-170, 197-200, 292-295, 314-317, 340-343) or a collapsed caret; there is no anchor>focus case and no `bold` backward case. So the issue #715 repro (bold `abcdef`, backward-select `cd`, un-bold, re-bold) is not covered end-to-end by any test, and if the summary happened to be caret-based/incorrect for backward ranges the new tests would still pass.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test exercises the real getRangeStyleSummary() on a backward (anchor>focus) selection, that there is no bold backward case, and that the issue #715 repro is not covered end-to-end. packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts is a direct counterexample the reviewer missed. It uses the real editor (initialize(container, store), line 91) with a real MemDocStore and contains zero vi.mock/vi.fn. selectTailBackward sets anchor.offset=4 / focus.offset=2 (lines 97-100), a genuine anchor>focus range; I confirmed at editor.ts:3868-3876 that _setSelectionForTest stores the range verbatim without normalizing order and moves the cursor to the focus, so the caret really lands at the offset-2 boundary that triggers the bug. Lines 151-153 assert on the real engine that getSelectionStyle().bold is true (preceding run) while getRangeStyleSummary().bold is not true (the range); lines 162-163 assert the inverse pairing. Lines 168-186 perform the #715 repro end-to-end: a real Cmd/Ctrl+B keydown on the mounted textarea over a backward range, asserted against the stored document via tailIsBold(store), covering both apply (formerly a silent no-op) and remove; line 188 pins the forward control case. The finding's own falsifiable prediction fails: a caret-based/incorrect summary for backward ranges would return bold:true at offset 2 in the setupEditor(true,false) case and break line 153 and the document assertion at line 174. The file is executed by the suite: packages/docs/package.json:36 runs "vitest --run" and packages/docs/vite.config.ts sets no include override, so the default test glob picks it up. The frontend component test may indeed stub the summary, but the blocking assertion here is that the behavior is tested nowhere, and it is tested at the engine level against the real implementation.
